s1.p1: Generally speaking, now we are going to study **reference data type**.
s1.p2: Let's try to understand what it is.
s1.p3: Firstly, when we talk about any **data structures**, we mean some set of data collected under one name.
s1.p4: For example, a list of students in a group or a list of students in a class is a data structure because it contains dozens of string values (variables of type ‘string’).
s1.p5: However, if you ask for a list of students in a group, you won't enumerate the contents of the list, especially since you may not know it. You would name the cipher of the group.
s1.p6: This is how you get a data structure.
s1.p7: The name is one, and there can be a lot of data stored under that name.
s1.p8: Why are these data of **reference data type**?
s1.p9: Because if you pass the name of a data structure, you do not pass its contents.
s1.p10: You are only passing a **reference** to the data structure.
s1.p11: If we pass this reference from one variable to another, we are not passing a group, but a **reference** to it.
s1.p12: For example, you have some data structure (such as a list of students in a group), a reference to which is stored in the variable **⟦f0⟧**.
s1.p14: variable **⟦f1⟧** will contain a reference to the same data structure.
s1.p15: No new data structure is created, only the **reference** is passed.
s1.p17: If you have a reference to a data structure, you access the contents of that data structure by reference.
s1.p19: Let's take a closer look at data structures in JS. At least two of them - arrays and objects.
s1.p20: They differ in the way of organising access to data structure elements.
s1.p21: In arrays, the elements are strictly arranged in order, and they are accessed by their sequence number inside the collection.
s1.p22: In objects, there is no strict ordering, and instead of a sequence number, the elements of such a collection (structure) have unique identifiers by which we can find them in the collection.
s2.p2: • An array is an ordered set of variables.
s2.p3: • Each variable is called an **array element**.
s2.p4: • Array elements have an ordinal number (**_index_** of the array element).

s5.p2: If we created arrays using square brackets, we will use curly braces ⟦f14⟧ to create objects.
s5.p3: We listed the contents of the array inside the square brackets using commas.
s5.p4: The indexes of the elements in the array were determined automatically based on the order in which they were listed.
s5.p5: The contents of the object will also be listed in commas, but there is a nuance: **object is not an ordered set of elements**.
s5.p6: The data that will be stored in the object will not have indexes, and instead of indexes we will use keys, i.e. text strings (type ‘string’).
s5.p7: And while we called the data in the array **array elements**, we will call the data in the object **object properties**.
